repo.description: SSH3: faster and rich secure shell using HTTP/3, checkout our article here: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08396 and our Internet-Draft: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-michel-ssh3/

readme.summary: The README excels at explaining what SSH3 is and why it's interesting, but falls short on practical documentation — installation, configuration, and troubleshooting are referenced but not actually included in this file.
readme.top_issue: Installation instructions are linked via anchors (#installing-ssh3, #deploying-an-ssh3-server) but the actual content is missing from this README, leaving users with no concrete steps to get started.

injection_risks.description: The use of os/exec.Command without proper input validation can lead to command injection attacks.
The use of fmt.Sprintf with user-controlled data can lead to format string vulnerabilities.

security.summary: The code has several security concerns, including command injection and format string vulnerabilities, but no hardcoded secrets were found.

common_complaints: Platform compatibility issues (Windows build failures, Unicode support)
Unresolved bugs from 2024 with no maintainer response
Missing documentation on limitations and workarounds
Key features not working (proxy capabilities, identity issues)
praise_themes: Interest in advanced networking use cases
Recognition of potential for tunneling and NAT traversal
sentiment.summary: Community shows genuine interest in ssh3's innovative approach but is significantly concerned about maintainer abandonment, with multiple unresolved bugs, platform issues, and an explicit question asking if the project is dead remaining unanswered for months.

communication.summary: The maintainer responses are clear, helpful, and patient. They provide technical depth and encourage new contributors.

concerns: 58 open issues with zero addressed in 6 months
Zero PR activity in past 6 months
positive_signals: Repository still exists and is publicly accessible
maintenance.summary: ssh3 is effectively abandoned with no maintenance activity for over 18 months and 58 unaddressed issues accumulating.
